title: reconcile detection output (`effect reconcile` stdout)
description: The escape-detection object `effect reconcile` prints — the computeEscapes result (observed-minus-declared) in bin/lib/effects.js. IMPORTANT: unlike the other kinds, the shipped `effect reconcile` verb emits this to STDOUT and does NOT append a ledger record — no code path writes a `kind_of_entry: reconcile` line, though KIND_AUTHOR reserves that kind for the producer. A normal run produces no escape (`any_escape: false`, empty `escapes`); both shipped examples were generated (a forced escape, and a planted dual-key record). Each escape carries `unit_id` and, for one release, the same value as `issue`; both are a non-empty string, or null on a `rejected-unit-key` escape or an escape with no resolvable unit. The subset validator cannot express string-or-null, so those two fields are untyped here and the rule is enforced by the CI test. Shape normative here; semantics in ../records.md.

any_escape.description: true iff at least one observed effect is uncovered by a declaration

signal.description: escaped-side-effect: observed effects no declare covers; rejected-unit-key: one ledger record carrying both issue and unit_id, reported on its own whatever the unit filter

issue.description: one-release alias of unit_id (same value): a non-empty string, or null (untyped: the subset validator cannot express string-or-null)

unit_id.description: the escape's work unit: a non-empty string, or null on a rejected-unit-key escape or an escape with no resolvable unit

seq.description: present on a rejected-unit-key escape: the seq of the dual-key record

event_seq.description: the events.jsonl seq of the escape when known; null from the ledger-only reconcile path (any type)
